questions.question: Name three things that can make one habitat different from another.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: how hot or cold it is, how wet or dry it is, the kind of soil or ground, how much sunlight reaches it, or whether it is on land or in water.

questions.question: Name three different habitats in South Africa and one animal or plant that lives in each.
questions.expected_answer: Any three, for example: the Kalahari desert, meerkats or gemsbok; grassland, blesbok; the forest near Knysna, the Knysna turaco or yellowwood trees; a wetland, hippos or crocodiles; the ocean, penguins or seals; fynbos, proteas.

questions.question: Explain why a meerkat could not live in Antarctica.
questions.expected_answer: A meerkat is suited to the dry, sandy Kalahari, where it digs burrows in the sand and finds insects to eat. Antarctica is covered in thick ice and is the coldest place on Earth, so the meerkat could not dig, keep warm or find its food there.
